title: Why The ISS Sees 16 Sunrises A Day
hook: You've never moved this fast: 27,600 kilometers an hour, right over your head.
closing: Even in space, you can't dodge a 24-hour day.
question: How much daylight did you get today?

segments.say: The ISS circles Earth at 27,600 kilometers an hour, far faster than a commercial jet.
The ISS orbits Earth every 93 minutes -- far faster than GPS or geostationary satellites.
Astronauts on the ISS see a new sunrise every single day, 16 times over.
